description: Unimos desarrollo de software, geología e ingeniería civil para resolver problemas reales del territorio. Usamos datos satelitales de la NASA, aprendizaje automático y desarrollo web para construir tecnología accesible orientada a la alerta temprana y la gestión de riesgos en tiempo real.
summary: Developed for the NASA/NISAR Hackathon, "Orbit Jump" is an immersive, bilingual (English/Spanish) pixel-art web game that combines interactive storytelling, geospatial data processing, and environmental education to make Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Earth observation data more accessible and engaging. Through a narrative-driven visual novel and top-down exploration maps, players follow Quipu, an Andean cat and planetary geologist from MIAUSA, aboard the Taruca Explorer as he returns from Proxima Centauri b to investigate environmental changes on Earth using NISAR satellite data. The project addresses the challenge of communicating complex scientific information by transforming geospatial insights into interactive, condition-gated trivia challenges across five vulnerable ecosystems, including the Peruvian Andes, the Amazon rainforest, and the Canadian Arctic. By connecting satellite observations with accessible gameplay, Orbit Jump helps students, educators, and communities explore real-world environmental phenomena such as deforestation, glacial retreat, and volcanic deformation. Ultimately, the project bridges the gap between scientific data and public understanding, fostering environmental awareness and encouraging informed engagement with Earth's changing ecosystems.
details:
A. Social, Environmental, and Technological Benefits

Social Benefits

  • Democratization of Scientific Knowledge: Orbit Jump facilitates access to specialized geospatial information by transforming Earth observation data into an interactive and understandable experience for users without prior technical knowledge.
  • Inclusive and Bilingual Education: By offering a platform in both English and Spanish, with a visual narrative inspired by graphic novels and pixel art, the project serves as an accessible educational resource for students, teachers, and the general public. It also helps bring environmental issues from different regions closer to local and international communities.
  • Development of Critical Thinking: Through interactive missions and challenges, users connect scientific information with real-world environmental situations, strengthening their analytical skills and understanding of the changes affecting our planet.

Environmental Benefits

  • Awareness of Environmental Issues: The project allows users to explore five study areas through information related to significant environmental phenomena: water resource availability in the Andes (Laguna San Nicolás), deforestation and illegal mining in the Amazon (Madre de Dios), ice loss and permafrost changes in the Canadian Arctic (Baffin Island), land subsidence and risks associated with sea-level rise in North Jakarta, and surface deformation in the volcanic region of Mount Aili.
  • Promotion of Environmental Awareness: By connecting satellite observations with their potential implications for ecosystems and surrounding territories, Orbit Jump helps improve understanding of environmental changes and highlights the importance of ecosystem conservation.

Technological Benefits

  • Integration of Geospatial Data into Web Environments: The project demonstrates the implementation of a geospatial data processing pipeline integrated into a gaming platform developed using web technologies such as HTML5, JavaScript, and Phaser.
  • Accessible Visualization of SAR Data: It facilitates the interpretation of information obtained through Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) from the NASA-ISRO NISAR mission by using visual representations, interactive maps, and gamification elements that make this data more accessible to non-specialized users.
  • Modular and Scalable Architecture: The project's structure allows for the incorporation of new study areas, datasets, and geospatial information layers, facilitating future expansions and the potential reuse of its approach in other Earth observation educational initiatives.

B. Contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and Space Missions

Orbit Jump aligns with the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Earth observation objectives of NASA and ISRO. By translating satellite observations into interactive educational experiences, the project contributes to the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):

SDG 13: Climate Action

  • Contribution: Through missions and interactive challenges based on NISAR satellite data, the game raises awareness of environmental changes associated with climate change. It allows users to explore phenomena such as ice loss and changes in the cryosphere in the Canadian Arctic (Baffin Island), encouraging a better understanding of climate-related environmental challenges and the importance of monitoring Earth's changing systems.

SDG 15: Life on Land

  • Contribution: The project promotes awareness of terrestrial ecosystem conservation by illustrating critical issues such as deforestation, illegal mining, and land degradation in the Amazon rainforest (Madre de Dios). By connecting satellite observations with these environmental challenges, Orbit Jump highlights the importance of protecting forests, biodiversity, and natural carbon sinks.

SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation

  • Contribution: By exploring water-related environmental challenges in the Peruvian highlands, particularly Laguna San Nicolás in the Andes, the project highlights the importance of freshwater resources and water security for local communities. Through geospatial information and satellite-based observations, users gain a better understanding of environmental changes that may affect the availability and preservation of water resources.

SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities

  • Contribution: By presenting the environmental challenges affecting North Jakarta's coastal region (Indonesia), the project explores land subsidence and urban vulnerability to coastal flooding and sea-level rise. This case helps users understand the importance of satellite-based monitoring in assessing urban environmental risks and supporting more resilient coastal communities.

SDG 4: Quality Education

  • Contribution: Orbit Jump promotes inclusive STEM education (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) and geospatial literacy. Through its bilingual narrative, interactive missions, and gamified learning approach, the platform makes advanced scientific concepts more accessible to students, educators, and the general public, regardless of their previous technical knowledge.

Contribution to Space Missions (NISAR – NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar Mission)

  • Public Engagement and Dissemination of Satellite Data: The NISAR mission is designed to observe changes in Earth's ecosystems, ice sheets, and land surfaces, while also supporting the study of natural hazards and environmental processes. Orbit Jump contributes to these objectives by transforming complex Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations into interactive visualizations, maps, and educational challenges. In doing so, the project demonstrates how satellite data and space-based technologies can be translated into accessible tools for scientific communication, environmental education, and public engagement.

C. Expected Community Impact

1. Objectives

Orbit Jump aims to make Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Earth observation concepts more accessible through an interactive, bilingual game. By combining storytelling, exploration, and selected NASA/ASF resources, the project seeks to help users understand how satellite observations can support the study of environmental change.

The project's main objectives are to:

  • Explain fundamental SAR concepts through dialogue, field activities, and trivia.
  • Present five environmental case studies from different regions of the world.
  • Integrate NISAR scene metadata and preview images into an accessible web experience.
  • Provide the main game content in both English and Spanish.
  • Encourage reflection on environmental challenges and the importance of scientific observation.

The achievement of these objectives can be assessed by determining whether users can navigate the five regions, complete the activities, access satellite information, and use the interface in both languages. Future user testing could also evaluate whether playing the game improves users' understanding of SAR technology and environmental monitoring.

2. Methodology

The development of Orbit Jump began with the identification of an educational challenge: making specialized Earth observation concepts understandable to people without prior technical knowledge.

The team selected five regions representing different landscapes and environmental topics. NASA and Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) resources were then consulted to identify relevant NISAR scenes and obtain their associated metadata, preview images, and scientific documentation. Python scripts were used to organize the case-study information and prepare selected resources for the web application.

In parallel, the team developed Quipu's story and created initial sketches for the game's characters and visual environments. The exploration and dialogue experience drew inspiration from the style and mechanics of Pokémon games. Generative AI tools were also used to refine visual proposals based on the team's original sketches and creative direction.

These concepts were integrated into a web prototype featuring a narrative introduction, a 2D exploration environment, field activities, trivia challenges, and a satellite information viewer. The application was refined through an iterative development process that included code revisions, build checks, and static code analysis.

The project combines real satellite resources with illustrative educational scenarios. The situations and numerical values used in some activities are intended for educational purposes and should not automatically be interpreted as measurements derived from the displayed satellite images.

3. Tools and Technologies

Orbit Jump combines satellite data resources, programming tools, and web technologies to create an interactive educational experience.

3.1. Software and Data Resources
  • NASA Earthdata and Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF): Used to access NISAR-related resources, including scene metadata, preview imagery, and supporting documentation.
  • asf_search: A Python package used to search the ASF catalog programmatically (documentation).
  • Python: Used to organize case-study information and prepare selected resources for the web application.
  • Pillow: Used to resize and convert selected preview images into web-friendly formats.
  • Leaflet: Used to display interactive maps and geographic information.
  • Three.js: Used to develop the interactive 3D orbital scene.
  • Git and GitHub: Used for version control and collaborative project management.
  • Generative AI tools: Used to support the refinement of visual proposals based on the team's original sketches and design concepts.
3.2. Programming Languages and Web Technologies

The application was developed using the following programming languages, frameworks, and technologies:

  • JavaScript and JSX: Used to implement the application's functionality and interface components.
  • React: Used to build the user interface through reusable components.
  • Vite: Used as the development environment and build tool.
  • HTML5 and CSS: Used to structure and style the web application.
  • Canvas API: Used to render the 2D exploration environment.
  • Python: Used for data organization and the preparation of satellite-related resources.
  • JSON and GeoJSON: Used to organize metadata, case-study information, and geographic features.
3.3. Hardware and Sensors

Orbit Jump is designed to run in a compatible web browser. Users do not need specialized hardware or a physical radar sensor to access the game. The development team used computers to create, test, and run the application.

The main satellite mission referenced in the project is NISAR, a joint mission developed by NASA and the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). The satellite carries two Synthetic Aperture Radar instruments: an L-band system provided by NASA and an S-band system provided by ISRO. The selected ASF resources used in Orbit Jump focus on NISAR L-band observations.

SAR is an active remote sensing technology. It transmits microwave signals toward Earth's surface and records the signals reflected back to the satellite. These observations can help scientists study changes in the Earth's surface and other environmental characteristics.

The project references NISAR-related resources available through ASF, including preview imagery and scene metadata. Although full GCOV products contain calibrated and terrain-corrected radar backscatter information, Orbit Jump uses selected preview images and metadata for educational exploration rather than claiming to process or analyze the complete scientific products within the game.

5. Location and Study Areas

Orbit Jump is a web-based project featuring five study areas selected to represent different landscapes and environmental contexts:

  • San Nicolás Lagoon and Namora, Peru: High-Andean water resources, wetlands, and surface conditions.
  • La Pampa and Madre de Dios, Peru: Forest loss, land-use change, and environmental monitoring in regions frequently affected by cloud cover.
  • Barnes Ice Cap, Canada: Ice and glacier dynamics in the Canadian Arctic.
  • North Jakarta, Indonesia: Coastal urban vulnerability, land subsidence, and flooding.
  • Hayli Gubbi, Ethiopia: Volcanic landscapes and surface deformation.

These locations provide diverse environmental contexts for introducing how radar observations can contribute to scientific research and environmental monitoring. Their representation in the game is intended for educational purposes and scientific communication.

6. Impact and Benefits

Orbit Jump seeks to make Earth observation information more accessible to students, educators, and other non-specialist audiences. Its bilingual content and interactive format provide opportunities to explore scientific concepts through visual storytelling and educational activities.

The project also aims to raise awareness of environmental challenges. By connecting its case studies with topics such as water resources, forest loss, ice dynamics, coastal vulnerability, and volcanic landscapes, the game can serve as a starting point for discussions about environmental monitoring and the role of satellite data in understanding changes on Earth.

These benefits represent the project's intended impact. Their educational and social outcomes should be evaluated through future user testing and feedback.

Connection to the Sustainable Development Goals

The project's educational and environmental themes align with several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):

  • SDG 4 — Quality Education: Promotes accessible STEM education and geospatial learning through an interactive, bilingual experience.
  • SDG 6 — Clean Water and Sanitation: Encourages awareness of water resources and environmental conditions in the Peruvian Andes.
  • SDG 11 — Sustainable Cities and Communities: Introduces coastal vulnerability, land subsidence, and flooding in urban environments.
  • SDG 13 — Climate Action: Encourages learning about environmental change and the use of satellite observations for monitoring.
  • SDG 15 — Life on Land: Raises awareness of forest loss, land-use change, and ecosystem conditions.

Orbit Jump also contributes to public engagement with topics addressed by the NISAR mission by presenting selected satellite resources in an accessible educational format. However, it is an independent educational prototype and should not be presented as an official NASA or ISRO monitoring product.

7. Results Achieved

The current version of the Orbit Jump prototype includes the following components:

  • English and Spanish content.
  • A 3D orbital introduction and a narrative sequence.
  • A 2D exploration environment featuring Quipu.
  • Five environmental case-study regions.
  • Field notes, interactive activities, and SAR-related trivia.
  • A world map and navigation controls.
  • A NASA/ASF viewer displaying selected scene metadata and preview imagery.
  • Python scripts for searching satellite scene metadata and preparing web resources.

The application has successfully passed build and static-analysis checks. These results confirm that the configured build process and code analysis run successfully. However, they do not, by themselves, demonstrate educational effectiveness or scientific validation.

The public game link, demonstration video, user feedback, and evidence of scientific validation remain to be added or documented, as applicable.

8. Conclusions and Future Improvements

Orbit Jump demonstrates how storytelling, visual design, web technologies, and Earth observation resources can be combined to create an educational prototype. It provides users with an opportunity to explore SAR concepts through interactive environments and activities.

One of the main lessons from the project is the importance of clearly distinguishing between real satellite resources, scientific interpretations, and illustrative game scenarios. Maintaining this distinction helps users understand the capabilities and limitations of the information presented.

Future development should focus on validating the geographic placement of radar preview images, reviewing the scientific explanations and illustrative values used in the activities, and testing the game with its intended audience. Additional improvements could include enhancing accessibility, completing the translation review, optimizing application performance, and establishing a reliable public deployment.
